race_context: Lawrenceburg Community School Corporation (LCSC) in Dearborn County runs Lawrenceburg Primary School, Central Elementary School, Greendale Middle School and Lawrenceburg High School and describes itself as 'home to about 2,000 students in kindergarten through high school' {lcsc_corp}. Its programs include a Spanish dual language immersion program and college credit through Vincennes University with a chance to earn an associate degree by graduation {lcsc_corp}.
Superintendent: Karl Galey, who has led LCSC since 2009 {ec_galey_2017}. He was still superintendent in January 2026 and at the board's Aug. 10, 2026 meeting {ec_lps_2026}{lcsc_min_20260810}.

The board has seven members elected from residence districts: District 1 (Lawrenceburg City) has three members, District 2 (Greendale) three and District 3 (Lawrenceburg Township) one, according to the district's board page {lcsc_board}. It meets the second Monday of each month at 6 p.m. at the Greendale Middle School Commons {lcsc_board}. In January 2026 the board re-elected Kevin Mollaun president, Regina Rybolt vice president and Bob Miller secretary, and set member pay at $4,090 a year plus $150 per regular session and $75 per special or executive session {lcsc_min_20260112}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the district lists four members whose terms run 2023-2026 — Erin Shepherd (District 1), Kevin Mollaun and Mark Knigga (both District 2) and Jacob Jump (District 3) — and all four filed for re-election {lcsc_board}{dearborn_cand}{in_list}. Rybolt, Fayla Nanz (District 1) and Miller (District 2) have terms through 2028 {lcsc_board}.

Seat count: the state list shows the District 2 race as 'vote for 1' with two candidates, but the district's board page shows both District 2 incumbents, Mollaun and Knigga, with terms ending in 2026, which suggests two District 2 seats are up; this could not be confirmed from a county sample ballot {in_list}{lcsc_board}. If two seats are being filled, the two District 2 candidates are not competing against each other. The Districts 1 and 3 races each have one candidate {in_list}.
Party labels: all four candidates are listed as Republicans on the state list; 2026 is the first year Indiana school board candidates could list a party {in_list}.

Budget and facilities (Sept.–Oct. 2025): the board held a public hearing on its proposed 2026 budget, capital projects plan and bus replacement plan on Sept. 22, 2025, where no one testified, and adopted project, preliminary determination and reimbursement resolutions for a building project by 7-0 votes {lcsc_min_20250922}. On Oct. 20, 2025 it adopted the 2026 budget 7-0, transferred education and operations funds to the Rainy Day Fund, and approved borrowing up to $400,000 through the Lawrenceburg Bond Bank to buy buses {lcsc_min_20251020}. A proposed 2027 budget schedule and a timetable for 'Unified Projects' were presented in August 2026 {lcsc_min_20260810}.

Teacher contract: a public meeting on the tentative teacher collective bargaining agreement was held Oct. 20, 2025, with ratification set for the Nov. 10, 2025 meeting {lcsc_min_20251020}. A required hearing on teacher compensation and bargaining with the Lawrenceburg Federation of Teachers was held Aug. 10, 2026, with no public testimony {lcsc_hear_20260810}.

Academics and safety: Galey told the board in September 2025 that IREAD-3 reading results at Central Elementary and Lawrenceburg Primary showed 96.8% passing (students can first take the test in second grade), and that the Greendale Redevelopment Commission had given $250,000 for school safety, part of it to be used as a local match for a state Secured School Safety grant {lcsc_min_20250908}. He reported a 98.2% graduation rate at Lawrenceburg High School for 2025 {lcsc_min_20251020}. In August 2026 Greendale Middle School joined a state Outcomes-Based Contracting adolescent literacy pilot {lcsc_min_20260810}.

The City of Lawrenceburg has given the district annual grants, including $245,000 a year and $350,000 for textbook fees as of 2019 {ec_city_2019}. LCSC is not among the districts that filed for a November 2026 property tax referendum with the state {dlgf_ref}.

Public input: board minutes from August 2025 through August 2026 record no citizen comments at regular meetings and no public testimony at budget and bargaining hearings {lcsc_min_20250908}{lcsc_min_20250922}{lcsc_min_20251020}{lcsc_min_20260810}. No candidate forum for the Lawrenceburg race was found.
